A4_S2_D1: ^Narrator: You approach a small settlement with tilled land and buildings which are similar to Dusk's in material.
^Narrator: Except… they are different in style. Less polished and ornamented; but more personal and lived-in.
^Amelia: We’re looking for some guy called Sillicone, right?
^Noelle: Cillian, actually. And since he's the head of their village, he shouldn’t be too hard to find.
A4_S2_D2: ^Narrator: You approach a girl who looks to be around your age.
^Narrator: She's busy wrangling some sort of small creature out of her hair.
^???: I told you not to pull on my hair.
^Narrator: It tries to bury itself further, only to be picked up and placed on the girl's shoulder instead.
^Narrator: She greets you warmly, before taking a moment to process the sight of you both.
^Clara: A dragon and a krakenfolk… You must be the travelers Cillian told us about!
choicehumanintro: ^Clara: Well, you’re in the right place… but he isn’t here at the moment. He went to visit my mentor, Ada.
^Amelia: By the way, what’s that thing in your hair?
^Narrator: Its a strange creaure that could roughly fit into one's hands, with a fluffy cotton-like coat.
^Clara: These little things? We use their wool to make thread! They don't talk much though, so don't mind them.
^Clara: While you're waiting for Cillain, why don't I give you a tour of town?
A4_S2_D3: ^Clara: We humans have lived here for as long as the other settlements, but a lot of newcomers arrived during Noah’s time, so we’re still working things out in terms of where extra hands will go.
^Clara: That being said, the Viridi and Ichthyos are descendants of humans. It’s just that some bloodlines adapted to the environment, and others didn’t.
^Clara: And of course, there’s the Krakenfolk who appeared after the whole Noah business.
^Amelia: The Krakenfolk moved to the seaside to live with the Ichthyos, right?
^Clara: Yup! They do say ‘may you live in interesting times,’ but the flood isn't one to scoff at!
A4_S2_D4: ^Narrator: Clara calls out to a pair who are packing items into crates.
^Clara: Hey Keira, Kiara! How are the supply preparations progressing?
^Keira: Good! At least so far. Supplies have been steadily moving up the mountains, however…
^Kiara: We’re a bit worried about the weather.
^Kiara: Superstition aside, the rain would make it dangerous to go uphill. But we’ll keep you posted!
^Narrator: Keira and Kiara finish nailing a crate closed and walk off, looking like they’re off to do something important.
^Clara: Hm… how much do you know about Noah's tale?
^Narrator: Clara explains that after Noah's altercation with the Great Disaster, those on Thavmia have been split between damning his actions and regarding it as an unfortunate fall of events.
^Clara: I'll spare you from the politics — things have calmed down after five-hundred years, but now that the floods are coming and the weather is strangely bad…
^Noelle: (People must be wondering if the storms are an answer to Noah's actions.)
^Noelle: So it doesn't normally storm on Thavmia?
^Clara: No. The most we'd get is heavy rain over the last centuries.
^Narrator: Clara snorts, not seeming to take offense.
^Clara: In any case, the weather has been… eventful, but at least no one's gotten hurt.
^Noelle: (The weather and Noah… this is probably putting the human settlement in an awkward position.)
^Noelle: (I wonder if any of them are direct descendants from that time?)
^Clara: Let's head west, towards the farm next!
